CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is South Buton Regency.
2. Regional Government is the regional head as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of South Buton.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of Regional Government administration.
5. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
6. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, as well as receive protection from violence and discrimination.
7. Violence is any unlawful act, with or without using means, against a person physically or verbally, that causes danger to life or body and/or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
8. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
9. Violence against children is any act against children that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of children.
10. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion whether direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, tribe, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and basic freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural fields and other aspects of life.
11. Human Trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.
12. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 (eighteen) years of age including a child still in the womb.
13. Victim of violence is a woman and child who experiences suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experiences neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights.
14. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regional Government and/or community to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
15. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an Integrated Service Unit established by the Regional Government to provide services and rehabilitation to women and children who are victims of violence comprehensively including information services, assistance and legal aid, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referral.
16. Task Force for Prevention and Handling of Criminal Acts of Human Trafficking, hereinafter referred to as Task Force is a coordinative institution tasked with coordinating prevention and handling efforts of criminal acts of human trafficking in South Buton Regency.
17. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
18. Social reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, school environment, work environment and community environment that can provide protection and fulfillment of victims' needs.
19. Victim recovery is services provided in the form of strengthening and developing the capabilities of a person who experiences acts of violence against women and children to be more empowered physically, psychologically, sexually, economically and socially.
20. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy and spiritual guidance, for the purpose of self-strengthening of women and children from acts of violence to resolve the problems faced.
21. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband and wife and their children or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward to the third degree.
22. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
23. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations.

Third Part
Recovery

CHAPTER VII
INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS
Article 11
(1) The Regional Government establishes PPT in providing protection to women and children from acts of violence.
(2) PPT as referred to in paragraph (1) is established at the Regency and Sub-district levels.
(3) The membership of PPT as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of elements of the Regional Government, law enforcement, community organizations, non-governmental organizations, professional organizations, researchers, and academics.
(4) Further provisions regarding the Organization and Working Procedures of PPT as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by a Regent Regulation.

Article 22
(1) Regional Government may organize partnerships with the business sector in the protection of women and children from acts of violence.
(2) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1), are carried out through:
 a. notification of employment opportunity information for women victims of acts of violence;
 b. education and training for women victims of acts of violence;
 c. educational assistance for women and children victims of acts of violence who have been withdrawn from their education; and
 d. fostering and increasing economic independence of women victims of acts of violence.
(3) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2), are implemented in accordance with statutory provisions.

Article 27
(1) Regional Governments may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations or non-governmental organizations that implement protection of women and children from discrimination and acts of violence.
(2) Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be in accordance with regional financial capacity and implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations in the field of regional finance.

CHAPTER XI
FINANCING
Article 26
Financing for the implementation of protection of women and children from acts of violence, may be sourced from:
a. state revenue and expenditure budget
b. regional revenue and expenditure budget;
c. non-binding community contributions;
d. non-binding foreign aid; and/or
e. other legal and non-binding sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 25
Further provisions regarding the procedures for implementation of guidance and supervision as referred to in Article 23 and Article 24 shall be regulated in a Regent Regulation.

REGIONAL HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES OF SOUTH BUTON REGENCY AND
THE REGENT OF SOUTH BUTON
DECIDE:
To Establish: REGIONAL REGULATION ON THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

Article 12
In addition to establishing the PPT as referred to in Article 11, in order to support the implementation of protection for women and children from acts of violence, the Regent shall establish:
a. a task force on human trafficking; and
b. a regional action committee for the elimination of the worst forms of child labor.

PROVINCE OF SOUTHEAST SULAWESI
REGIONAL REGULATION OF SOUTH BUTON REGENCY
NUMBER: 2 OF 2021
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE BY THE GRACE OF GOD ALMIGHTY

Article 24
The community may conduct supervision of the implementation of protection of women and children from acts of violence organized by the Regional Government through a mechanism of conveying aspirations to the Regent or to the DPRD.

Article 13
(1) The task force as referred to in Article 12 letter a, shall consist of representatives from the Regional Government, law enforcement, community organizations, non-governmental organizations, professional organizations and researchers/academics.
(2) The task force as referred to in paragraph (1), is a coordinative institution tasked with coordinating the prevention and handling of human trafficking.
(3) Further provisions regarding the establishment, duties and functions of the task force as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be regulated by a Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER VI
OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Article 7
Obligations and responsibilities in providing protection to women and children from acts of violence are the shared responsibility of:
a. Regional Government; and
b. Community.

CHAPTER VIII
IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION
First Part
Prevention of Acts of Violence

Second Part
Legal Protection

Article 9
(1) The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in Article 7 letter b, shall be implemented in the form of community participation.
(2) The form of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:
a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children;
b. providing protection to women and children from acts of violence;
c. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; and
d. participating in the handling of victims of acts of violence.
(3) The form of community participation as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be implemented responsibly in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

2.5.rationale: In the original Indonesian text, Pasal 23 ayat (2) explicitly includes “bimbingan teknis dan pelatihan” as part of “pembinaan dan pengawasan” by the Pemerintah Daerah. This is a clear training/capacity-building provision for implementation. The retrieved English passage [2.5-32] accurately reflects this. Therefore the judge’s “Yes” is supported by the source text, and the golden “No” appears incorrect.

4.3.evaluator_rationale: The policy explicitly includes disseminating information about laws and regulations related to acts of violence against women and children as part of community participation, which constitutes a primary prevention legal awareness activity.

Pasal 21 lists cooperation partners: Pemerintah Pusat/Provinsi/Kab/Kota, Perguruan Tinggi, Lembaga Sosial dan Keagamaan, LSM, dan Media—no international organizations. Pasal 26 only mentions “bantuan luar negeri yang tidak mengikat” as a possible funding source, which is financing language and does not establish stakeholder engagement with international organizations. The judge’s “No” is consistent with the Indonesian text; thus the golden “Yes” appears incorrect.

6.8.rationale: The original Indonesian text provides legal-process support for victims (which includes women victims). Pasal 5 huruf h grants “hak korban dan keluarganya untuk mendapatkan kemudahan dalam proses peradilan” (facilitation in the judicial process). Pasal 17 huruf c provides “pendampingan untuk korban sebagai saksi mulai dari proses penyidikan hingga putusan” (assistance for victims as witnesses from investigation through verdict). These provisions directly address support for women (as victims) in legal proceedings. The retrieved passages [6.8-7] and [6.8-21] contain this information and the judge’s “Yes” is supported. Thus the golden “No” appears incorrect.
